provenance.abstraction_rationale: Derived from report br_pytorch_pytorch_120803 for torch.batch_norm_update_stats: an empty input tensor on Linux CPU caused a floating point exception, addressed by adding a non-empty input check.
unresolved_information: No reported_diagnosis root-cause claim was mapped in the report; the mechanism was inferred from the resolution patch and PR title.
No explicit expected behavior statement was mapped in the report.
No explicit historical oracle statement was mapped in the report.

historical_conditions.statement: The input tensor passed to torch.batch_norm_update_stats had shape [0,0] (zero elements).
The invocation occurred on Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS x86_64) with CUDA unavailable.

defect_mechanism.description: In the CPU batch_norm_update_stats implementation, n_input is set to input.size(1) and n is computed as input.numel() / n_input. For an input tensor of shape [0,0], both input.numel() and n_input are zero, so the division computes 0 / 0 and causes a floating point exception before any input validation.

observed_failure.description: Calling torch.batch_norm_update_stats with an input tensor of shape [0,0] terminated with 'Floating point exception (core dumped)'.

historical_observations.statement: The issue is reproducible on Linux (Ubuntu), but not on Mac M1.
A proposed test expects torch.batch_norm_update_stats with an empty input to raise RuntimeError with the message 'input tensor must have at least one element, but got input_sizes = [0, 1]'.
